title: A Novel Image-Graph Heterogeneous Fusion Framework for Static IR Drop Prediction
problem: IR drop analysis is critical for IC reliability but computationally challenging at ultra-deep-submicron scales. Current CNN-based approaches neglect power delivery network (PDN) global spatial features and cell-instance topological information.
motivation: As IC designs scale to extreme complexity, IR drop verification becomes a bottleneck; more accurate, efficient prediction methods are essential for design closure.
method: Image-Graph Heterogeneous Fusion (IGHF) framework combining CNN and GNN branches. CNN branch (Power ScaleFusion UNet) uses Long-range Local-detail Encoder (LLE) and Hierarchical Adjacent Compensation Group (HACG) for multi-scale spatial power feature extraction and adaptive fusion. GNN branch uses Cell Voltage Aware (CVA) module to aggregate PDN topological features from heterogeneous neighbors. Transfer learning enables few-shot adaptation to real circuits.
key_novelty: Dual-branch CNN-GNN architecture integrating spatial power delivery features with topological PDN information, achieving superior IR drop prediction accuracy through complementary feature extraction.
contributions: LLE module for multi-scale power feature extraction
CVA module for topological PDN aggregation
Transfer learning for few-shot real circuit adaptation

metrics.accuracy: 24.6% error reduction vs MAUNet, 55.0% vs IREDGe

limitations: Evaluation on specific circuit datasets; generalization to diverse technology nodes and design styles not fully explored.
primary_theme: CNN-GNN fusion for IR drop prediction in large-scale ICs
